div.head: Blas 3
div.ab: Gyf he ðonne að forðbringan ne mæge 7 he ðonne ful sy, stonde on ðara yldestana manna dome, hwæðer he hlif age ðe náge, þe to ðære byrig hyron.
Gif he ðone að forþbringan ne mæg ⁊ he þonne fúl sy, stande on þæra yldesta manna dome, hweþer he lif áge þe nage, þe to ðære byrig hyran.
Si iusiurandum perficere nequeat, ut reus (non direxerit et culpabilis) sit, stet in seniorum hominum iudicio, utrum uitam habeat uel non habeat, qui ad ipsam curiam obediunt (pertinent).
Gif he þone að forðbringan ne mæg and he þonne fúl sy, stande on þæra yldesta manna dome, hweðer he lif áge þe nage, þe to þære byrig hyran.

Wenn jener solchen Eid nicht zu Stande zu bringen vermag, und er also schuldig dasteht, so stehe es in der Entscheidung der angesehensten Männer, die zu jener Gerichtsstätte gehören, ob er das Leben behalte oder verliere.

If he cannot bring forward such an oath, and he thus stands guilty, let it rest with the judgment of the most senior men who belong to that place of court [borough] whether he keeps his life or loses it.
If he [the accused] cannot produce the oath and is proved guilty, the chief men of the borough shall decide whether his life shall be spared or not.
If he cannot produce the oath and so be guilty, let it be in the judgement of the most senior men that belong to the borough whether he have life or not.
div.note: In all MSS Forfang follows without a break, perhaps taken from the same royal law. With ‘bringan’ a new quire begins in B, which was mistakenly bound at the front (now p. 1). Liebermann compares II As 20.1.
